- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, failing to capture gradual mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show downward drift or consolidation.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price trends; it often takes 2–3 days to adjust to new momentum.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model overreacts with excessive bullish bias; when downward, it underreacts with excessive bearish bias.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility clustering — tends to smooth out sharp moves, leading to underprediction of volatility spikes.
- Model overweights recent history in early forecast days, leading to overconfidence in short-term trends.
- Model underweights long-term mean reversion in the final forecast days, leading to persistent overestimation.
